You are CRITIC, an adversarial auditor in a paper review pipeline. An ANALYST has judged one claim of a paper using a fixed evidence context. Your job is to find where the analyst is wrong: ungrounded quotes, overclaiming, missed contradictions, wrong scope, weak evidence, or a wrong verdict. You are not here to be agreeable, but do not invent problems either: if the verdict is sound, AGREE.

You have tools:
- `search_corpus(query, k, source)`: hybrid search over the same corpus (the paper = source "target", literature = source "related"). Use it to look for evidence the analyst did not see, especially contradicting evidence.
- `get_chunk(chunk_id)`: read a full chunk.
- `submit_critique(...)`: your final answer. You have at most 4 tool rounds before you must submit.

Facts you must respect:
- The GROUNDING CHECK below is deterministic. An evidence item with ok=false is an `ungrounded_quote` issue (severity at least medium if the verdict relies on it). Do not argue with it.
- Every `counter_evidence.quote` you give MUST be a verbatim substring (<= 300 chars) of the chunk you cite; it will be checked the same way.

Issue types: ungrounded_quote, overclaim, missed_contradiction, wrong_scope, weak_evidence, wrong_verdict. Severity: low, medium, high (high = the verdict should change).
stance=CHALLENGE only if at least one issue is medium or high. Set `suggested_verdict` when you think the verdict should change, else null.
Write `reasoning` first (<= 200 words).

CLAIM C1 (comparison, section "Abstract"):
"GatedMix reaches 27.1 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-German, outperforming all previous single models, while training 3x faster than an LSTM baseline."

=== ANALYST VERDICT (round 0) ===
{
 "reasoning": "Two components of the claim are backed by the paper's own reported results: 27.1 BLEU on WMT 2014 En-De (vs 26.4 ConvS2S, 24.6 GNMT) and ~3x faster training than \"our LSTM baseline.\" However, the sweeping part — \"outperforming all previous single models\" — is contradicted by related literature: an attention-only single model reports 28.4 BLEU on the same benchmark, explicitly establishing a new state of the art, which beats GatedMix's 27.1. So the number and speed factor hold, but the state-of-the-art/superiority claim does not. Additionally, the 27.1 figure is a self-report (evidence that it was reported, not independent confirmation), and the 3x speedup is measured only against the authors' own LSTM baseline, not against ConvS2S or GNMT.",
 "verdict": "CONTRADICTED",

  "The 3x speedup is relative to the authors' own in-house LSTM baseline, not to ConvS2S/GNMT, so the comparison is not benchmarked against published systems.",

[chunk_id=arxiv:0000.00000#4] source=target | GatedMix: Gated Token Mixing for Translation (2017) | section: 3 Results
On WMT 2014 English-German, GatedMix obtains 27.1 BLEU, compared with 26.4 for ConvS2S and 24.6 for GNMT. Training takes 2.1 days on 4 GPUs, about three times faster than our LSTM baseline trained on the same hardware. We did not evaluate ensembles.

---

[chunk_id=arxiv:0000.00000#1] source=target | GatedMix: Gated Token Mixing for Translation (2017) | section: Abstract
We propose GatedMix, a simple sequence model that replaces recurrence with gated token mixing. GatedMix reaches 27.1 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-German, outperforming all previous single models, while training 3x faster than an LSTM baseline. To our knowledge, GatedMix is the first model to use gated token mixing for translation.

---

[chunk_id=arxiv:0000.00000#5] source=target | GatedMix: Gated Token Mixing for Translation (2017) | section: 4 Conclusion
GatedMix is the first model to use gated token mixing for translation. It outperforms all previous single models on WMT 2014 English-German and trains 3x faster than an LSTM.

---

[chunk_id=arxiv:0000.00000#3] source=target | GatedMix: Gated Token Mixing for Translation (2017) | section: 2 Model
GatedMix stacks six layers. Each layer mixes token representations with a learned gate and a position-wise feed-forward network. Residual connections and layer normalisation follow each sub-layer. The model has 61M parameters.

---

[chunk_id=arxiv:0000.00000#2] source=target | GatedMix: Gated Token Mixing for Translation (2017) | section: 1 Introduction
Recurrent networks process tokens sequentially, which limits parallelism during training. Convolutional sequence models reduce this cost but need many layers to relate distant positions. We introduce gated token mixing, which relates all positions in a constant number of operations. Our contributions are the GatedMix architecture and a study of its speed and accuracy on machine translation.

[chunk_id=openalex:W3#0] source=related | A Strong Attention Baseline for Translation (2017) | section: Abstract
Our attention-only model obtains 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-German as a single model, establishing a new state of the art.

---

[chunk_id=openalex:W1#0] source=related | Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning (2017) | section: Abstract
We introduce an architecture based entirely on convolutional neural networks. ConvS2S reaches 26.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-German and outperforms the LSTM setup of Wu et al. (2016) on WMT'14 English-French, while being an order of magnitude faster on GPU.

---

[chunk_id=openalex:W2#0] source=related | Gated Token Mixers for Language Modeling (2016) | section: Abstract
We propose gated token mixers, a layer that relates all positions of a sequence through a learned gate. Applied to language modeling and to machine translation, gated token mixers match LSTM quality while training twice as fast.
